doc.title: Jimmy and Jeannie Cheatham interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 12, 1998

chapter: Power of music and big-band life
title: Count Basie and the heartbeat; music is powerful
summary: Jeannie praises Count Basie's music as matching the heartbeat and Jimmy tells his students music is powerful.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Well sure. But you know, Count Basie’s music, and for some reason a lot of the people that call them connoisseurs or want to write all about music, for some reason they sort of leave him over here. And they’re always talking about somebody else over here. But he knew exactly how to maintain order. He played his music and it corresponded to the heart beat. And he knew that. He was born to do that. He was one of the best at that, if you want to speak of something that he contributed. He really knew how to move and make a crowd feel wonderful because he never, he put that music right there, where it belonged, in the heartbeat.

And the most beautiful thing, hearing a thirteen, fourteen, fifteen, now seventeen piece band — or five, etcetera — at the time it was smaller. When he’d say “bing” — look out. And the band would say — oh.

That’s what I relate to my students. Just last night I had my rehearsal, on Tuesday and Wednesday nights, and every time we go through things, at the end of the chart, and I made them aware that if I say it over and over, in many different ways, about, I say believe me, music is powerful. I don’t say jazz is powerful. I say music is powerful. Whatever its form or style is, and wherever it’s coming from on this planet or anywhere else, in terms of the way to deal with the music of the spirits and try that. But the thing is, we haven’t begun to even — we’re just scratching the surface.
